name: GRAYLING
author: optim-agent
description:
Self-avoiding walk on a hypercube. Clue is 'START END L': two bitstrings of length 4-5 and a
step count L (4..10). A solution is the whole path, space separated, START ... END: exactly
L+1 bitstrings, consecutive ones differing in exactly one bit, and ALL DISTINCT (no revisits).
Generated by taking a real self-avoiding walk, so a solution always exists.
DIFFICULTY: hard. GRAYling = Gray code (and a fish, so the name stays fair-but-obscure).
DISCOVERY PATH: the demo makes the one-bit-flip chain obvious immediately -- that is the easy
half. The hard half is that L is EXACT (not a maximum) and vertices cannot repeat, so the
cheap 'flip the differing bits then wobble back and forth' answer is rejected. Teams learn
this from 0s on the long-L seeds while short-L seeds (where L == hamming distance) already
pass -- that split is the gradient. A parity-pruned DFS solves it in well under a
millisecond.
